The '''Qatar Emiri Air Force''' ({{langx|ar|القوات الجوية الأميرية القطرية |Al-Quwwat Al-Jawiyah Al-Amiriyah Al-Qatariyah}}) (QEAF) is the air arm of the [[Qatar Armed Forces|armed forces]] of the state of [[Qatar]]. It was established in 1974 as a small aerial support wing, although in modern times it has evolved into a potent, well equipped force. The QEAF is headquartered at [[Al Udeid Air Base|Al-Udeid Air Base]]<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Cordesman|first1=Anthony H.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XWg1mvPuhkUC&pg=PA150|title=Gulf Military Forces in an Era of Asymmetric Wars|last2=Al-Rodhan|first2=Khalid R.|date=2007|publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group|isbn=978-0-275-99400-6|language=en}}</ref> in [[Doha]]; the current commander is Major General (Pilot) Mohammed bin Abdullah Al-Dosari.

==History==
In March 1967, in response to the British announcement that it would withdraw its armed forces from the [[Persian Gulf]], Qatar set up armed forces, creating the Qatar Public Security Forces Air Wing, equipped with two [[Westland Whirlwind (helicopter)|Westland Whirlwind]] helicopters. In 1971, it acquired a combat capability when it purchased three ex-RAF [[Hawker Hunter]] jet fighters, which remained in use until 1981. It was renamed the Qatar Emiri Air Force in 1974.<ref name="ai988 p136">''Air International'' September 1988, p. 136.</ref>

The air force began a major expansion in 1979, when it ordered six [[Dassault/Dornier Alpha Jet|Alpha Jet]] trainer/light attack aircraft. This was followed by orders for 14 [[Mirage F1]] supersonic jet fighters in 1980, which were delivered between 1980 and 1984. Twelve [[Aérospatiale Gazelle|Gazelle]] helicopters, armed with [[HOT (missile)|HOT anti-tank missiles]] were received from 1983. Also in 1983, the air force took over the Qatar Police Air Wing.<ref name="ai988 p136,9">''Air International'' September 1988, pp. 136, 139.</ref>

In 1991, the Qatari Air Force took part in the [[Gulf War]] on the side of the allies.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2013/09/15/middleeast/gulf-war-fast-facts |title=Gulf war fast facts|publisher=CNN Editorial Research|year=2020|access-date=15 December 2020 |url-status=live|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201112020744/https://edition.cnn.com/2013/09/15/world/meast/gulf-war-fast-facts/index.html |archive-date=12 November 2020}}</ref>

In 2005, the Air Force participated in Exercise Eagle Resolve, along with Qatari medical services and emergency medical teams to build interoperability with their US counterparts. The US [[26th Marine Expeditionary Unit]] took part in this exercise to validate the nation's crisis management plan prior to hosting the [[2006 Asian Games]].

Other acquisitions have been for an order of 59 [[AgustaWestland AW139|AW139]] helicopters.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120720163806/http://www.asd-network.com/press_detail/17039/Qatar_Armed_Forces_Sign_Contract_for_18_AW139_Helicopters.htm|title=Qatar Armed Forces Sign Contract for 18 AW139 Helicopters}}. Asd-network.com. Retrieved on 2011-03-28.</ref> The helicopters are used for utility tasks, troop transport, search and rescue, border patrol, special forces operations, and law enforcement. Three additional aircraft were ordered in March 2011 for [[Medical evacuation|Medevac]] services.<ref>[http://www.agustawestland.com/news/qatar-armed-forces-order-three-ems-configured-aw139s "The Qatar Armed Forces Order Three EMS-Configured AW139s"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140505194406/http://www.agustawestland.com/news/qatar-armed-forces-order-three-ems-configured-aw139s |date=May 5, 2014 }} ''Agusta Westland'' 21 March 2011</ref>

By 2010, the Qatar Emiri Air Force's personnel strength was at 2,100 and its equipment included the Mirage 2000-3EDA, the SA 342L Gazelle, and the [[Boeing C-17 Globemaster III|C-17A Globemaster III]]. Aircraft either flew out of al-Udeid field or [[Doha International Airport]] and received training from British instructors. In January 2011, the Air Force evaluated the [[Eurofighter Typhoon]], the [[Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II]], the [[Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet]], the [[McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle]] and the [[Dassault Rafale]] to replace, and significantly expand from, its then-current fighter inventory of twelve Dassault Mirage 2000-5s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.avascent.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/11/Defense-News-AJ-Article-12.13.pdf |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191214060329/https://www.avascent.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/11/Defense-News-AJ-Article-12.13.pdf |url-status=dead|archive-date=2019-12-14|title=US Bid Delays Qatar Jet Competition}}</ref>  In May 2015, the QEAF awarded the contract for 24 Dassault Rafale fighters worth €6.3 billion ($7 billion).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/c985c8c8562c4bed96073f77fa16c931 |title=France sells 24 Rafale fighter jets to Qatar in a $7 billion deal|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150518095819/http://www.apnewsarchive.com/2015/France-sells-24-Rafale-fighter-jets-to-Qatar-in-a-7-billion-deal/id-c985c8c8562c4bed96073f77fa16c931 |archive-date=2015-05-18|work=Associated Press News|date=2015-04-30|first=Sylvie|last=Corbet}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/gulf/qatar-air-force.htm |title= Qatar Emiri Air Force (QEAF) |publisher=Global Security |access-date= 4 May 2015 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150228003426/http://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/gulf/qatar-air-force.htm |archive-date= 28 February 2015 |url-status= live |df= dmy-all }}</ref>

In July 2012, the Qatar Emiri Air Force ordered a complete pilot training system from Pilatus centering upon the PC-21. The package included ground-based training devices, logistical support and maintenance in addition to 24 PC-21 aircraft.

In June 2015, the QEAF ordered four additional C-17s, to supplement the existing four delivered in 2009 and 2012.

In September 2016, the sale of up to 72 F-15QAs to Qatar was submitted to the US Congress for approval.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-qatar-usa-jets-idUSKCN1175GQ |title=U.S. set to approve sales of Boeing fighters to Qatar, Kuwait - sources|publisher=Reuters|date=1 September 2016|access-date=29 September 2016|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160930105304/http://www.reuters.com/article/us-qatar-usa-jets-idUSKCN1175GQ |archive-date=30 September 2016|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-09-28/fighter-jet-sales-to-gulf-allies-backed-by-u-s-after-long-wait |title=Fighter Jet Sales to Gulf Allies Backed by U.S. After a Wait|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|publisher=Bloomberg|date=29 September 2016|access-date=29 September 2016|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160928223834/http://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-09-28/fighter-jet-sales-to-gulf-allies-backed-by-u-s-after-long-wait |archive-date=28 September 2016|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref> The deal (for 36 planes plus an option for 36 more),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.defenseone.com/business/2016/10/us-allows-qatar-buy-f-15s-and-seals-19b-sale-jetliners/132249/ |title=US Allows Qatar to Buy F-15s — and Seals a $19B Sale of Jetliners |publisher=Defense One|date=October 11, 2016}}</ref> valued at US$21.1 billion, was signed in November 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.combataircraft.net/2016/11/18/qatar-and-kuwait-fighter-deals-signed-off/ |title=Qatar and Kuwait fighter deals signed off|publisher=Combat Aircraft|date=18 November 2016|access-date=18 November 2016|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20161119112506/http://www.combataircraft.net/2016/11/18/qatar-and-kuwait-fighter-deals-signed-off/ |archive-date=19 November 2016|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

In September 2017, the QEAF ordered 24 Typhoon fighter jets from the UK.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/17/09/2017/UK-to-supply-Qatar-with-24-Typhoon-fighter-jets |title=UK to supply Qatar with 24 Typhoon fighter jets |access-date=2017-09-17 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170917173355/http://www.thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/17/09/2017/UK-to-supply-Qatar-with-24-Typhoon-fighter-jets |archive-date=2017-09-17 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In December 2017, the QEAF ordered 12 additional Rafale fighter jets from France, with an option for 36 more.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.france24.com/fr/20171207-qatar-france-visite-emmanuel-macron-rafale-airbus-blindes-metro-ratp-sncf |title=Visite d'Emmanuel Macron au Qatar: Doha achète 12 Rafale et 50 Airbus|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171213010823/http://www.france24.com/fr/20171207-qatar-france-visite-emmanuel-macron-rafale-airbus-blindes-metro-ratp-sncf |archive-date=2017-12-13|publisher=France24|date=2017-12-07|language=fr}}</ref>

In August 2018, Qatar announced the construction of a new air base: [[Dukhan / Tamim Airbase]], named after Emir [[Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani]]. In addition to the new air base, [[Al Udeid Air Base]] and [[Doha International Air Base]] were planned to expand in order to accommodate aircraft on order.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Binnie |first1=Jeremy |title=Qatar announces new airbase |url=https://www.janes.com/article/82634/qatar-announces-new-airbase |website=IHS Jane's 360 |access-date=2 September 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180829154633/https://www.janes.com/article/82634/qatar-announces-new-airbase |archive-date=2018-08-29 |location=London |date=29 August 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The country includes three different types of [[fighter jet]]s from three different countries in its fleet, each requiring distinct maintenance and repair contracts, which some have criticized as an unusually complex arrangement for such a small nation. This was a "strategic [[Hedge (finance)|hedge]]", but also a significant logistical challenge.<ref name=cal>{{cite web |last1=Larson |first1=Caleb |title=F-15s, Eurofighter Typhoons and Dassault Rafale Fighters: Qatar’s Air Force Is Now Fighting Iran |url=https://www.19fortyfive.com/2026/03/f-15s-eurofighter-typhoons-and-dassault-rafale-fighters-qatars-air-force-is-now-fighting-iran/ |language=en |date=4 March 2026}}</ref>

Recent disclosures, the latest of which was published in November 2024, uncovered corruption and bribery related to Qatar's arms contracts over the past decade. Several companies engaged in business partnerships with Qatar have been ordered to pay penalties in connection with bribery charges.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-16 |title=Defense contractor to pay $252M penalty to resolve Qatar bribery charges |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/defense-contractor-to-pay-252m-penalty-to-resolve-qatar-bribery-charges/7824918.html |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=Voice of America |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rohde |first=Ruth |date=2024 |title=Raytheon’s Dirty Business in Qatar (Sham Contracts) |url=https://corruption-tracker.org/case/raytheons-dirty-business-in-qatar |access-date=2024-12-02 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Arms trade corruption – what do we know? |url=https://worldpeacefoundation.org/blog/arms-trade-corruption-what-do-we-know/ |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=World Peace Foundation |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Dou |first=Eva |date=2024 |title=Raytheon to pay $950 million to settle fraud, Qatar bribery charges |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2024/10/16/raytheon-fraud-qatar-bribery/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-16 |title=Defense contractor RTX agrees to pay more than $950 million to resolve bribery, fraud claims |url=https://apnews.com/article/raytheon-defense-contractor-qatar-bribery-3d495d19979bd17740a68fecdeda2f36 |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

On 10 October 2025, US Secretary of Defense [[Pete Hegseth]] announced an agreement with Qatar to establish a QEAF facility at [[Mountain Home Air Force Base]] in [[Idaho]]. It is planned to host a contingent of F-15QAs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bsky.app/profile/atrupar.com/post/3m2tumte7pj2b |title=@atrupar.com on Bluesky}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/hegseth-announces-new-qatari-air-force-facility-idaho-following-partnership-gaza-peace-deal |title=Pentagon agrees to host Qatari F-15 fighter jets and pilots at Idaho air base|first=Bonny|last=Chu |date=10 October 2025|website=Fox News}}</ref>
